paper.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning

request.focus: We propose a dual-tower architecture that combines line plots and normalized delay embeddings within a shared language model

passages.text: • Complementary representations for time-series reasoning. We establish complemen- tary representation as a design principle for TSLMs, motivated by the observation that quantitative readout requires the original measurement frame, whereas reasoning about temporal dynamics benefits from factoring it out. • A dual-view time-series language model. We propose a dual-tower architecture that combines line plots and normalized delay embeddings within a shared language model. Dedicated visual encoders, compact visual tokens, and multi-level feature fusion integrate temporal structure with the original measurement frame. • State-of-the-art TSLM performance. With an 8B backbone, our model outperforms all evaluated dedicated TSLMs on TSRBench, achieving 53.2% accuracy versus 36.7% for the strongest baseline. It also

passages.text: that combining these complementary views is par- ticularly useful beyond basic perception, where reasoning, prediction, and decision-making require models to exploit temporal structure while remaining grounded in the observed measurements. Building on this representational principle, we design a dual-tower TSLM in which each visual view is processed by a dedicated encoder. We retain Qwen3-VL’s native vision encoder, initialized from SigLIP-2 (Tschannen et al., 2025), to process line plots, and introduce a dedicated DINOv3 encoder (Sim´ eoni et al., 2026) for delay embeddings, allowing each view to develop a specialized visual representation before interacting with the language model. The resulting visual features are compressed into a compact set of tokens, 230 for the line plot and 64 for the delay embedding, and concatenated as input to the language model. Beyond this input-level fusion, we adopt Deep- Stack (Meng et al., 2024) to inject multi-level visual features into the early

passages.text: temporal reasoning, whereas TS-Reasoner (Yu et al., 2026b) aligns representations from a pretrained time-series foundation model with an LLM. In parallel, benchmark studies have shown that general-purpose vision-language models can reason surprisingly effectively over time series presented as line plots (Cai et al., 2024; Yu et al., 2026a), providing an alternative to explicitly learned time-series interfaces. Despite these diverse strate- gies, existing TSLMs predominantly expose the language model to a single primary representation of each temporal signal. concepts.name: 互补表示（complementary representations）
concepts.summary: 一种针对时序语言模型（TSLM）的设计原则：定量读出需要保留原始测量框架，而关于时间动态的推理则受益于把该框架因子化出去，因此需要同时提供保留不同信息、具有不同不变性的多个视图。

evidence.quote: Our work instead treats representation as a source of complementary in- ductive biases, jointly providing views that deliberately preserve different information and exhibit different invariances.

concepts.name: 双塔架构（dual-tower architecture）
concepts.summary: 每个视觉视图由专用编码器处理，再在共享语言模型中融合的架构：折线图走原生视觉编码器，延迟嵌入走专用 DINOv3 编码器。

evidence.quote: We propose a dual-tower architecture that combines line plots and normalized delay embeddings within a shared language model.

concepts.summary: 现有 TSLM 普遍只让语言模型接触每个时序信号的单一主表示；本文以互补表示原则针对这一局限。
